name: tin
desc: Threaded, NNTP-, and spool-based UseNet newsreader
why: A threaded UseNet newsreader is an old-school environment and a living door into NNTP and spool-based news that few people have seen.

brief.what_it_is: tin is a threaded UseNet newsreader that reads news over NNTP or from a local news spool. The homepage describes it as a newsreader for a variety of platforms. The package installs seven executables: tin, rtin, metamutt, tinews.pl, url_handler.pl, w2r.pl and opt-case.pl. The homepage does not say what each one does, so the brief does not describe them.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated motivation. It presents tin as the development headquarters for an established newsreader, with a stable release, manpages, a change log and a mailing list.
brief.standout: The project runs its own mailing-list archive that can be read via NNTP, which fits a newsreader for news. It also has entries for Debian bug logs, a Debian security tracker and Free Translation Project domains for translating the program and its manpages.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage announces TIN 2.6.6 (stable) released on August 23, 2026, and its footer says 'Last changed: 2026-08-23'. Those are the only dates I saw, and I did not check the source repository.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage. The README and manpages were not fetched, so there are no usage examples, install steps or platform list. The homepage's links to manpages, screenshots and the stable-branch code are labels without URLs in the fetched text, so I did not follow them. The scout note's 'old-school environment' framing is the scout's, not the project's.
quotes: tin is a threaded NNTP and spool based UseNet newsreader for a variety of platforms.
fetch_log: http://www.tin.org: fetched OK; homepage text only, no README content or command examples on this page
